chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'From which mosque do I enter the state of Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah?' He said, 'From whichever mosque you wish.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, he should trim his moustache, clip his nails, and perform Ghusl.' He narrated this until the end of the chapter.

key_terms.أُحْرِمُ: I enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended acts of purification and grooming before entering Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of the Miqat for Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah, allowing the pilgrim to assume the state from any mosque, while simultaneously prescribing the Sunnah acts of grooming (trimming the moustache and clipping nails) and ritual bathing (Ghusl). It highlights the integration of physical purification with spiritual intention, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the preparation for Hajj.
